Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html

## Oracle [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#oracle)

This page covers the plain-language Oracle connection check that `release.sh` runs on Citadel and that `squire doctor oracle` runs from your terminal, and the two opt-in Oracle-ready Docker images Squire ships for local work. Next, read [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html) to wire the release script into the dashboard, or [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) to run the app on the real images.

### The connection check [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#the-connection-check)

The release runs an Oracle connection check (`oracle-check.php`) after PROCTOR and before the smoke test. It is a report, never a gate: a finding prints in the deployment log and the release goes on. When the app does not use Oracle (no `ORACLE_*` settings) it prints nothing.

It checks, in order:

1. the settings are present,
2. the host resolves,
3. the port answers within 3 seconds,
4. the `oci8` driver is loaded,
5. the login works.

The check stops at the first failure, so a bad port never costs a login attempt. Only setting names are ever printed, never values.

Settings: `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` (Easy Connect `host:port/service`, or a full `(DESCRIPTION=...)` descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`.

### `squire doctor oracle` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#squire-doctor-oracle)

`vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle` runs the same plain-language Oracle connection check that `release.sh` runs on Citadel, from your terminal or `sail php vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle`. It reads the `ORACLE_*` settings from the environment and the app's `.env`, prints setting names and never values, and stays silent when the app has no Oracle settings. Add `-v` for the client version.

### Oracle-ready images (local) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html#oracle-ready-images-local)

Apps that talk to Oracle need the Instant Client and the `oci8` extension. Squire ships two opt-in Docker recipes that carry both, so nobody compiles them by hand:

- `squire/oracle-sail:<php>`: Laravel Sail's own runtime plus the Oracle install. In your `docker-compose.yml`, swap the service's `build:` block for `image: squire/oracle-sail:8.4` and keep the rest of the service as Sail wrote it; the image keeps Sail's entrypoint contract, including the `WWWUSER` UID remap.
- `squire/oracle-parity:<php>`: the official `php:<php>-cli-bookworm` image with the extensions Citadel apps use (intl, ldap, soap, zip, gd, pdo_mysql, mysqli, bcmath, pcntl, exif, redis, imagick), Composer and git, plus the Oracle install. This is the flavor WELD's `compose.oracle.yaml` points its services at. It runs as a non-root `app` user whose UID is a build argument (`APP_UID`) and can still be overridden at run time.

The names above are the local names of `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh`. The published images live in the group's `images` project (the stack's shared image registry; Squire's own GitLab has no container registry), at `<registry>/enterprise-apps/images/squire-oracle-parity:8.4` and `<registry>/enterprise-apps/images/squire-oracle-sail:8.4` (`<registry>` is the registry address of the images project shown on its Container Registry page), plus `:8.4-<squire version>` for a fixed one. CI publishes them when a Squire version is tagged, multi-arch (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64); a Sail app swaps `build:` for `image:` with that path.

Both flavors download Oracle's Instant Client Basic Light at build time under Oracle's license and never commit it: the install script pins the exact SHA-256 of each zip. Oracle does not publish a 21.x client for arm64, so the line differs per architecture: linux/amd64 gets 21.7.0.0.0 and linux/arm64 gets 19.32.0.0.0.

```
scripts/oracle-image-build.sh --flavour sail --php 8.4        # or: --flavour parity
scripts/oracle-image-test.sh --flavour all --platform linux/amd64
```

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html

## The portable image [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#the-portable-image)

Citadel builds its own image, and `.squire/Dockerfile` mirrors that one and stays a mirror. Everywhere else (OpenShift, Coolify, a plain `docker run`, ADR-0010's portable path) an app needs an image it can take with it: the code inside, one image for every process type, and no assumption that it starts as root. That is `.squire/portable.Dockerfile`. A squire packs one saddlebag that fits every horse.

Read [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) first for the base image, and [Queue workers on Citadel](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html) for the Citadel side of the same worker.

### What differs from the Citadel mirror [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#what-differs-from-the-citadel-mirror)

Both start from the same base, the same `php.ini` and `php-web.ini`, and YOUR `build.sh`. Then:

|  | `.squire/Dockerfile` (Citadel mirror) | `.squire/portable.Dockerfile` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code | mounted at `/citadel/src` | baked in at `/citadel/src` |
| Process types | Apache only (`CMD ["apache2-foreground"]`) | web, worker, scheduler or migrate, by argument or `SQUIRE_ROLE` |
| User | starts as root, Apache drops to `prisoner` | `USER 10001:0`; any UID in group 0 works |
| Port | 80 | 8080 (`SQUIRE_PORT`, else `PORT`) |
| Logs | files under `/citadel/logs`, rotated | stdout and stderr |
| Stop signal | `SIGWINCH` (the base's) | `SIGTERM`, a graceful stop for every role |
| Release | `scripts/release.sh` on the running container | its install-and-build half at image build; config cached at container start; migrations from the `migrate` role |
| opcache | checks files (a bind mount changes them) | never checks files (`SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE=0`) |

Citadel never reads the portable files, so nothing here changes a Citadel app.

### Build it [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#build-it)

From the app root, with the kit at the root (where Sourdough and `squire init` put it):

```sh
docker build -f .squire/portable.Dockerfile --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<base image> -t my-app .
```

With the kit in a subfolder (WELD keeps it in `deploy/`), the context is still the app root; say where the kit is:

```sh
docker build -f deploy/.squire/portable.Dockerfile --build-arg SQUIRE_KIT_DIR=deploy --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<base image> -t my-app .
```

`BASE_IMAGE` is the real Citadel image or the fallback base (`.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`), pushed to a registry the platform can pull from. The build runs `scripts/release.sh` with the run-time steps off: Composer without dev packages, the frontend build, the writable folders, and nothing that needs the app's settings (no migrate, no optimize, no restart, no smoke test, and PROCTOR's gate belongs in CI on this path). Composer's and npm's downloads go through a BuildKit cache mount, so a rebuild fetches only what changed.

`node_modules/` goes once the frontend build is done, in the same build step, so no layer keeps it: the image ships the built assets (`public/build/` for a Vite app), and none of the four roles runs Node. The kit has no server-side rendering role, so nothing at run time needs those packages. An app that does read `node_modules/` at run time (a page that serves a file straight out of it, say) keeps it with `--build-arg SQUIRE_KEEP_NODE_MODULES=1`; better still, copy that file into `public/` in the build script.

`portable.Dockerfile.dockerignore` sits next to the Dockerfile, so Docker reads it for this build only: `.env` files, `auth.json`, `secrets`, keys, `.git`, `vendor/` and `node_modules/` never reach the build context, let alone a layer.

### Run it as an arbitrary UID [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#run-it-as-an-arbitrary-uid)

OpenShift runs a container as a random UID that has no `/etc/passwd` entry and is always in group 0 ([OKD: support arbitrary user IDs](https://docs.okd.io/latest/openshift_images/create-images.html#use-uid_create-images)). The image follows that recipe: the folders the app and Apache write (Apache's run, lock and log folders; `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` for Laravel) belong to group 0 and are group-writable (`chgrp -R 0` then `chmod -R g=u`). Try it the way OpenShift would:

```sh
docker run -d --name my-app-web --user 1000123:0 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true \
  --env-file .env -p 127.0.0.1:8081:8080 my-app
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8081/up
```

It needs no capability at all: it never starts as root, and 8080 is not a privileged port. A raw PHP app that writes somewhere else names those folders at build time with `--build-arg SQUIRE_WRITABLE_DIRS="var/cache var/log"`.

### One image, four roles [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#one-image-four-roles)

The first argument picks the role, else `SQUIRE_ROLE`, else `web`:

| Role | Runs | Replace it with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web` | Apache and mod_php on `SQUIRE_PORT` (else `PORT`, else 8080) |  |
| `worker` | `php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600 --sleep=3` | `SQUIRE_WORKER_COMMAND` |
| `scheduler` | `php artisan schedule:work` | `SQUIRE_SCHEDULER_COMMAND` |
| `migrate` | `php artisan migrate --force`, once per release | `SQUIRE_MIGRATE_COMMAND` |

Arguments after the role are passed on (`worker --queue=high,default`), and options alone go to the `SQUIRE_ROLE` process, so a platform that sets only `command: ["--queue=high"]` beside `SQUIRE_ROLE=worker` gets what it means. Any other first argument is run as a command: `docker run --rm my-app php artisan about`.

The Laravel roles run `php artisan optimize` first, so config, routes and views are cached for the container's own environment when it starts, never at build time, where they would freeze the build machine's settings. `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=0` skips it (the same switch `scripts/release.sh` reads). A route closure that cannot be serialized fails `route:cache` and stops the container with Laravel's message; skip optimize while you fix the route, and know the release on Citadel stumbles on the same route.

A raw PHP app has no `artisan`, so it names its own worker and scheduler; the role stops with a plain message (exit 64) when the command is missing, instead of starting something that is not there. `migrate` with nothing to migrate succeeds, so the services that wait for it still start.

A bad setting stops the container before anything starts, with exit 64 and one line that says what to change: a port that is not a number, a port below 1024 for a user that is not root, an unknown role, an empty named command.

### Compose: the `portable` profile [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#compose-the-portable-profile)

`docker-compose.squire.yml` carries the same four roles as a profile beside the parity stack. A plain `up` still starts only the Citadel parity services; the profile starts nothing until you name it:

```sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.squire.yml --env-file .env.squire --profile portable up -d --build web worker scheduler
```

- **One image.** Every service builds and runs `squire-local/portable:<project>`; they differ only in `SQUIRE_ROLE`.
- **migrate** runs once, after MySQL is healthy, and the other three wait for it to finish successfully (`restart: "no"`).
- **web** is published on `127.0.0.1:${SQUIRE_PORTABLE_HTTP_PORT:-8081}`, beside the parity proxy on 8080.
- **worker** comes back after `--max-time` ends it, through `restart: unless-stopped`.
- **scheduler** sets `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=none`: Sourdough's Laravel shapes schedule a short queue worker by default, and here the worker service has the queue.
- Every service runs as `${SQUIRE_PORTABLE_USER:-10001:0}` with `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `no-new-privileges`, and memory and process limits, reads the app's settings from `${SQUIRE_PORTABLE_ENV_FILE:-.env}` (never baked in), and logs to stderr.

The settings are in `.env.squire.example` under "the portable image". WELD sets `SQUIRE_PORTABLE_CONTEXT=..` and `SQUIRE_KIT_DIR=deploy`, because its app sits one folder up from the kit.

### Deploys and signals [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#deploys-and-signals)

Every role stops on `SIGTERM`, the signal every platform sends. Apache's graceful stop is `SIGWINCH`, so for `web` the entrypoint stays as a small init that turns `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` into `SIGWINCH` and exits with Apache's status: requests in flight finish. `worker` and `scheduler` exec PHP directly, and `queue:work` finishes its current job on `SIGTERM` before it exits ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#queue-workers-and-deployment)). A platform that replaces containers on a deploy therefore starts the new ones on the new code, and needs no restart signal; `scripts/release.sh`'s `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART` step stays the Citadel answer, where the container lives on across releases. Keep each job's timeout below its connection's `retry_after`, as on Citadel.

### Health [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#health)

The image's `HEALTHCHECK` runs `squire-entrypoint health`. For `web` that is `health.php` on the port Apache listens on; `SQUIRE_APP_DIR` (set in the image) points `health.php` at the app root even when the kit sits in a subfolder. `worker`, `scheduler` and `migrate` have no endpoint to ask, so they are healthy while their process runs, and the platform's restart policy covers a process that dies.

### Not covered here [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#not-covered-here)

- The base image's `EXPOSE 80` still shows in the image metadata (a Dockerfile cannot take back an inherited port); nothing listens there.
- Publishing the image is the platform's or the CI's job; this kit builds it.
- The Citadel mirror, `vhost.conf` on 80 and the fallback base's `EXPOSE 80` are unchanged on purpose: a change there would claim a parity Citadel does not have.

### How it was checked [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#how-it-was-checked)

`tests/PortableImageTest.php` reads every portable file and runs the entrypoint in bash with stand-ins for `php`, `apache2-foreground` and `id`: each role, the argument and setting precedence, the refusals, the health check, the secrets loader, and `SIGTERM` reaching Apache as its graceful stop. On 2026-11-08 the image was also built and run for real, for a raw PHP app and for WELD: `docker run --user 1000123:0` answered `/up` with 200 on 8080 from Apache running as `1000123:0`; the compose profile ran `migrate` (exit 0), then `web`, `worker` and `scheduler` healthy as `1000123:0`; the worker ran a queued job; and `docker stop` ended all three in about two seconds, each with exit 0. On 2026-11-09, for 0.10.2, Buildah 1.43 (short-name mode enforcing) refused the 0.10.1 fallback base at its `COPY --from=composer:...` and built the new one with no build arguments; WELD's portable image then built on it under Buildah and under Docker with no `node_modules/` left in it (1.38 GB with `SQUIRE_KEEP_NODE_MODULES=1`, 1.20 GB without), and served `/up` and its front page with the built assets, as `1000123:0`.

### Next [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html#next)

Read [Queue workers on Citadel](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html) for the timeout rule both paths share, or [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html) for what the base and the kit harden.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html

## Queue workers on Citadel [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#queue-workers-on-citadel)

Laravel apps on Citadel dispatch jobs to a queue, but the platform runs no queue worker: one container per app, Apache in front, and nothing that keeps a long-lived `php artisan queue:work` alive. A queue with no worker is a promise with no keeper. This page covers what works today (a short worker driven by the scheduler), how a release restarts workers, what has not been tested yet, and the request text for the supervised worker we want from the Citadel team. Finish [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html) first if the app is not wired up yet.

### What works today [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#what-works-today)

Laravel's own guidance is that a permanent `queue:work` needs a process monitor to keep it running ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#supervisor-configuration)), and Citadel has none. So the worker rides the one thing every app already runs: the scheduler's single cron entry, which runs as the app user each minute ([scheduling](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/scheduling#running-the-scheduler)). An app that already schedules tasks has this entry; the worker reuses it, so nothing new runs on the server.

```cron
* * * * * cd /path-to-your-project && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
```

The schedule then starts a short worker every minute. In `routes/console.php` (Laravel 11+, where the scheduling docs put the task schedule):

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schedule;

Schedule::command('queue:work --stop-when-empty --max-time=50')
    ->everyMinute()
    ->withoutOverlapping(10);
```

Each piece is documented:

- `--stop-when-empty` processes all jobs and then exits gracefully, the option Laravel documents for a container that should shut down once the queue is empty ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#processing-all-queued-jobs-and-then-exiting)).
- `--max-time=50` caps a run at 50 seconds, so a run started before a release cannot outlive the code it booted with ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#processing-jobs-for-a-given-number-of-seconds)).
- `everyMinute()` runs the task on each scheduler tick ([scheduling](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/scheduling#schedule-frequency-options)).
- `withoutOverlapping(10)` skips the tick while the previous run is still going. The lock lives in the cache and expires after 24 hours by default; the explicit 10-minute expiry bounds a lock that a crashed run leaves behind ([scheduling](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/scheduling#preventing-task-overlaps)).

Because every run boots fresh and exits, there is no stale code and no memory growth between runs. The trade is latency: a job waits for the next minute tick, and a busy queue drains one burst per minute.

Apps that Sourdough generates in its Laravel shapes ship this already, behind one switch. `config/worker.php` reads `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE`: `scheduler` (the `.env.example` default) schedules the short worker above, and `none` schedules nothing, for an app whose worker a supervisor or a separate container runs. Their task adds `--tries=3`, so a failing job stops after three attempts instead of retrying on every tick ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#dealing-with-failed-jobs)), and `tests/Feature/QueueWorkerScheduleTest.php` checks both modes. An app built by hand can copy the same three pieces.

Warning

Keep every job's timeout below its connection's `retry_after`, at least several seconds shorter. If a job is still processing past `retry_after`, the connection releases it back onto the queue and another run picks it up, so the job runs twice. The worker's `--timeout` is 60 seconds by default, the shipped `retry_after` is 90, and a job may name its own timeout with the `Timeout` attribute ([worker timeouts](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#worker-timeouts), [job expiration](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#job-expiration)). Job timeouts need the PCNTL extension in the image ([max job attempts and timeout](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#max-job-attempts-and-timeout)). Give jobs a finite number of tries: `--tries=0` retries forever, and a permanently failing job would then spin the queue every minute.

With the `database` driver the jobs live in a table that Laravel's default migration creates (`0001_01_01_000002_create_jobs_table`); an app without it generates one with `php artisan make:queue-table` ([queues](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues)).

### Deploys [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#deploys)

Workers do not notice new code until they restart, so a release restarts them ([queue workers and deployment](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/queues#queue-workers-and-deployment)). Laravel documents two commands, and the current release has both:

- `php artisan queue:restart` tells every worker to exit gracefully after its current job, so no job in flight is lost. The restart signal is stored in the cache, so the app needs a working cache driver.
- `php artisan reload` terminates the long-running services (queue workers, Reverb, Octane) in one command; outside Laravel Cloud you configure the process monitor that restarts them yourself ([deployment](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/deployment#reloading-services)).

For the short worker above, the restart is mostly belt-and-braces: a run started before the release ends within its 50-second cap regardless, and the command makes sure it ends now instead of finishing the rest of the window on old code. For a supervised worker the restart is the whole mechanism, because the process never exits on its own.

Squire's `scripts/release.sh` does this for you in its Laravel block, after `laravel migrate` and `laravel optimize` and before the Oracle check and the smoke test: the code is checked out and optimized, the smoke test has not run yet, and a worker restarted here comes up on the new code before the release declares success. The step runs `php artisan reload` where Laravel has it, and otherwise `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt`, each only when that command exists. It is report only (a failed restart is a warning), and `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0` turns it off. See [The release script](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html) for the step order.

### Off Citadel: a worker process type [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#off-citadel-a-worker-process-type)

On a platform that runs more than one process per app (OpenShift, Coolify, raw Docker), the worker is its own container from the same image: [The portable image](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html) runs as `worker` (`php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600 --sleep=3`, the command the request below asks Citadel for) and as `scheduler` (`php artisan schedule:work`), picked by `SQUIRE_ROLE`. The scheduler there sets `QUEUE_WORKER_MODE=none`, so the short worker above is not scheduled beside the real one. A deploy replaces the containers, so no restart signal is needed, and the timeout rule above holds on both paths.

### Not yet tested on Citadel [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#not-yet-tested-on-citadel)

The short worker is the stack's plan, not a measured fact: the combination of `--stop-when-empty`, `--max-time` and `withoutOverlapping` puts three documented features together, and it has not been run on Citadel yet. How fast a queue actually drains, how the cron entry behaves on the platform, and what the logs look like are all unmeasured, and the Citadel test is tracked separately; this page will say what it found when it lands.

### The supervised worker we are asking for [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#the-supervised-worker-we-are-asking-for)

The text below is ready to send to the Citadel team. It asks for the long-lived worker Laravel expects, with the restart hook that makes deploys safe.

```text
Request: a supervised queue worker per app

We would like a supported way to run one long-lived process per app, kept alive by a process monitor that restarts it when it exits.

What it runs:

    php artisan queue:work --sleep=3 --tries=3 --max-time=3600

One worker per app, more where an app needs the throughput.

Why: Laravel's queue worker is a long-lived process that a process monitor must keep running, and it does not pick up new code until it is restarted. Today our apps run a short worker from the scheduler every minute, which works but is a stopgap: a job waits up to a minute for the next tick, a run that fills its minute overlaps the next one (the overlap guard then skips ticks and adds more delay), and the framework reboots every tick.

Restart on deploy: the Quick Update post-script (where scripts/release.sh already runs) would call php artisan reload, which terminates the worker after its current job finishes; the monitor then starts it again on the new code. The stop is graceful: on SIGTERM the worker finishes the job it is processing before it exits.

Timeouts: each job's timeout stays below the connection's retry_after (at least several seconds shorter), so a frozen job is killed before the queue retries it and runs twice. The image needs the PCNTL extension for job timeouts.

Logs: worker output where the app's other logs are, viewable in the dashboard, so a dead worker is visible instead of silent.

Cache: the restart signal is stored in the application cache, so the app's cache store must survive the restart (the file store does, inside one container).
```

### Next [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/queue-workers.html#next)

Read [The release script](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html) for the step order a restart fits into, or [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html) for the dashboard steps that make the cron entry exist.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html

## Quick start [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

A squire carries the kit and readies the armor before the knight charges, and this page is that ride. Four numbered steps take a new app from `composer require` to a checked, deploy-ready setup; do them in order, then follow a next link.

### 1. Install Squire [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#1-install-squire)

Squire is a dev dependency. It runs on your machine or in CI, not on Citadel; what lands on Citadel is the scripts it writes. PHP `^8.3`, tested on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5.

```bash
composer require waynestate/squire --dev
```

### 2. Run squire init [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#2-run-squire-init)

`init` picks the target from your app: `laravel` when there is an `artisan` file, `raw` without one, or set it yourself with `--target`. It detects a Vue/Inertia layer from `package.json` and adds the layer's release script and Node 22 parity service.

```bash
vendor/bin/squire init
```

The full option set:

```text
vendor/bin/squire init   [--path=.] [--target=auto|raw|laravel|static] [--only=release|parity] [--check] [--force]
```

`init` never overwrites a file you edited, or a file it did not write, unless you pass `--force`. It records a SHA-256 of each file in `.squire.json`. `--only=release` writes just the Citadel scripts, `--only=parity` just the local setup. The release installs from the lock file, so when the app has no `composer.json` or no `composer.lock`, `init` ends with a "Heads up" line: commit both before the first deploy (`composer init`, then `composer update`), or the release stops at step 1.

### 3. Run squire doctor [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#3-run-squire-doctor)

```bash
vendor/bin/squire doctor
```

`doctor` checks an app against the best practices a machine can decide. The lock file, composer audit and MySQL 5.6 checks are owned by PROCTOR; `doctor` hands off to it (S50) instead of repeating them.

Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` findings (`init --check`: drift; `update`: an edited file still differs from the template; `doctor`: a failed rule), `2` the tool itself could not run.

### 4. Commit .squire.json [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#4-commit-squire-json)

Commit the `.squire.json` record file. `update` reads it to know which files Squire wrote, and `init --check` reports when your copies have drifted from the templates (depend, do not copy).

### What you built [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `build.sh` | Citadel's build hook: system packages only, POSIX sh, runs as root with no app source. No Composer, no npm. |
| `deployments/001-first-release.sh` | Runs once per app: calls the release script with the smoke test off (Apache is not up yet). |
| `scripts/release.sh` | The idempotent release: preconditions, `composer install --no-dev` from the lock file, audit, PROCTOR's deploy gate (`proctor gate`, a report by default, a stop with `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), frontend build, Laravel `migrate --force` and `optimize`, an Oracle connection check (a report, never a gate), `/up` smoke test. Use it as the Quick Update post-script as well. |
| `health.php` | Citadel's health check (`["php","health.php"]`): one HTTP request to `/up`, never boots the framework. |
| `oracle-check.php` | The plain-language Oracle connection check the release runs: settings, host, port, driver, login. A report, never a gate; silent when the app has no `ORACLE_*` settings. |
| `public/up.php` | Raw PHP and static: the endpoint that answers `ok`. Laravel has `/up` built in. |
| `public/index.php` | Raw: the front controller that serves `public/` files safely and hands the rest to the app's entry. Static: the one that serves the committed site with HELMET's headers. Never written over an app's own. |
| `public/.htaccess` | Raw: sends every request but `index.php` and `up.php` to the front controller. Static: routes every request that is not a real file to it. |
| `.npmrc` | Vue layer only: sets `min-release-age=1` for the frontend install. |
| Vue `docker-compose.squire.yml` | Vue layer only: the common parity compose plus a Node 22 service for frontend tooling. |
| `docker-compose.squire.yml`, `.squire/`, `.env.squire.example`, `scripts/parity.sh`, `scripts/parity.ps1` | Local parity. |

Every shell script uses `set -euo pipefail` (`build.sh` uses `set -eu`, because Citadel runs it with `/bin/sh`), prints a `[squire] ==> step N: ...` marker for each step, and can be run twice with the same result.

### Next steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Raw PHP app](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html)
- [Static site](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html)
- [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html)
- [Release script](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html)
- [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html)
- [Doctor](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html)
- [Update and drift](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html)
- [Commands](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html) and [Files](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html)

## Raw PHP app [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#raw-php-app)

This page is for apps without a framework: what `squire init --target=raw` writes, and how the front controller decides what to serve, what to refuse, and what to hand to your entry. If you have not run `init` yet, start with the [quick start](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html).

### What the raw target writes [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#what-the-raw-target-writes)

A raw PHP app (`--target=raw`, the default without an `artisan` file) gets a front controller, `public/index.php`, and an `.htaccess` that sends every request to it.

### The front controller's three answers [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#the-front-controller-s-three-answers)

- a real file in `public/` (CSS, images, fonts, an HTML page) is served with its type, an ETag and an hour of cache, with HELMET's headers when HELMET is installed, and HELMET's CSP nonce on every `<script>` of an HTML page;
- a 404 for a dot file (`.htaccess`, `.git`), a NUL byte, a path that climbs out of `public/`, any `.php` or `.phar` other than the front controller, and any file that is not a site asset (a `.sql` dump, a `.bak`, a `.md` with no `.html` beside it);
- everything else goes to the app's entry: `app.php` beside `public/`, or the file `SQUIRE_APP_ENTRY` names (relative to the app directory, for example `src/bootstrap.php`). A `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` always goes to the entry.

### SQUIRE_APP_ENTRY [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#squire-app-entry)

The entry is the only PHP file the front controller runs, and it must sit inside the app directory and end in `.php`; anything else is a plain 500 that names `SQUIRE_APP_ENTRY` and no path. The entry boots its own HELMET with its own settings: the front controller boots HELMET (citadel preset) only for the answers it gives itself, never before the entry, so HELMET is never booted twice.

### App-owned files [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#app-owned-files)

An app that already has its own `public/index.php` or `public/.htaccess` keeps it: `init` reports the file as `app-owned`, never records or overwrites it (not even with `--force`), and `init --check` does not count it as drift. Delete your copy and run `init` to take Squire's. A front controller Squire wrote is tracked like any other file.

### public/up.php [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php-app.html#public-up-php)

`public/up.php` answers on its own, because the `.htaccess` lets Apache run it directly. The path checks and the MIME map are the static target's, and the tests keep the two in step; see [Static site](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html) for that side.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html

## The release script [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#the-release-script)

This page walks through `scripts/release.sh`, the one common script every app gets, in the order its steps run. It is the artifact that lands on Citadel; read [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html) first if you have not wired the dashboard yet.

### What it is [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#what-it-is)

`scripts/release.sh` is the idempotent release: preconditions, `composer install --no-dev` from the lock file, audit, PROCTOR's deploy gate (a report by default, a stop with `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), frontend build, Laravel `migrate --force`, `optimize` and the restart of the long-lived processes, an Oracle connection check (a report, never a gate), and a `/up` smoke test. It runs from the first-release hook and from the Quick Update post-script (user `citadel`, script `./scripts/release.sh`).

Its neighbors in the kit:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `build.sh` | Citadel's build hook: system packages only, POSIX sh, runs as root with no app source. No Composer, no npm. |
| `deployments/001-first-release.sh` | Runs once per app: calls the release script with the smoke test off (Apache is not up yet). |
| `health.php` | Citadel's health check (`["php","health.php"]`): one HTTP request to `/up`, never boots the framework. |
| `oracle-check.php` | The plain-language Oracle connection check the release runs: settings, host, port, driver, login. A report, never a gate; silent when the app has no `ORACLE_*` settings. |

Every shell script uses `set -euo pipefail` (`build.sh` uses `set -eu`, because Citadel runs it with `/bin/sh`), prints a `[squire] ==> step N: ...` marker for each step, and can be run twice with the same result.

### Idempotence and step markers [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#idempotence-and-step-markers)

Safe to run twice: every step repeats with the same result (S10). Each step prints a marker such as `[squire] ==> step 4: composer install from the lock file, without dev packages`, and a failure names the step: `[squire] FAILED at step N (name): reason` with the exit code and line number. A release script that is not idempotent is just a rehearsal that happens to ship.

### Step by step [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#step-by-step)

1. **check preconditions**: refuses to run as root unless `SQUIRE_ALLOW_ROOT=1` (files it creates could not be written by the web process); requires `composer.json` and `composer.lock` in the app root (the lock file is the release, S13); requires `php` and `composer` on PATH; resolves the framework (`auto` detects Laravel from `artisan`, otherwise `raw`); requires `.env` when `SQUIRE_REQUIRE_ENV` resolves to `1` (Laravel always does); picks the smoke URL (`http://127.0.0.1:80/up` for Laravel, `http://127.0.0.1:80/up.php` for raw PHP).
2. **create writable directories**: creates the `SQUIRE_WRITABLE_DIRS` entries, or `storage bootstrap/cache` for Laravel by default.
3. **package download caches**: skipped when `SQUIRE_CACHE_DIR=off`, which leaves Composer's and npm's own defaults alone. Otherwise it creates `$SQUIRE_CACHE_DIR/composer` and `$SQUIRE_CACHE_DIR/npm` (the default `.cache/squire` is relative to the app root, an absolute path is used as is), writes a `.gitignore` of `*` and an `.htaccess` of `Require all denied` into the folder when they are missing (so git ignores the cache without touching the app's own `.gitignore`, and Apache never serves it), and points `COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` and `npm_config_cache` at the two folders unless the environment already sets them (a value the host set wins). The app folder survives a Citadel Update, the container home does not, so the next release installs from what this one downloaded. It notes both cache paths in the log.
4. **composer install from the lock file, without dev packages**: logs the Composer version (it moves at every container start, S58), then `composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist`.
5. **composer audit**: `composer audit --locked --no-interaction`. By default (`SQUIRE_COMPOSER_AUDIT=report`) a non-zero exit prints a warning and the release goes on; `fail` stops it, `skip` skips it.
6. **PROCTOR gate**: see below. It runs before the frontend build and the migrations, so an enforced no-go stops the release before it touches the database.
7. **frontend install and build**: skipped without a `package.json` or with `SQUIRE_NPM=skip`. With `package-lock.json` it runs `npm ci --prefer-offline` (with `--ignore-scripts` when `SQUIRE_NPM_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=1`); with `pnpm-lock.yaml` it runs `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; with neither lock file it fails, telling you to commit one or set `SQUIRE_NPM=skip` if the built assets are committed. The packages named in `SQUIRE_NPM_REBUILD` then run their own install scripts, and nothing else does. With npm older than 11.10 and a `min-release-age` line in `.npmrc`, it notes that this npm ignores the line (the lock file still decides what installs). It then runs the `build` script (or `SQUIRE_NPM_BUILD_SCRIPT`) when `package.json` defines it.
8. **laravel migrate** (Laravel only): `php artisan migrate --force` when `SQUIRE_MIGRATE=1`.
9. **laravel optimize** (Laravel only): `php artisan optimize` when `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=1`. After this the config is cached and `.env` is no longer read, so `env()` works only inside `config/` (S16).
10. **laravel restart long-lived processes** (Laravel only): skipped when `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0`. When `php artisan reload --help` succeeds it runs `php artisan reload`; otherwise it runs `php artisan queue:restart` and `php artisan schedule:interrupt`, each only when its own `--help` succeeds, and notes the skip when neither exists. A failing command is a warning naming the command and its exit code, and the release goes on. A worker that keeps running holds the old code in memory until it restarts, so the step sits after the caches are built and before the smoke test.
11. **check Oracle (never fails the release)**: runs `php oracle-check.php` when the file exists, and notes a skip when it does not (the app does not use Oracle).
12. **check opcache (never fails the release)**: reports whether the web server sees changed files by itself. With the kit's default (`SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE=1`, files checked every 2 seconds) it is a note. With `0`, meant for an image that bakes its code in, Apache keeps serving the PHP it compiled before this release until it restarts, so after a release with Apache running this is a warning naming `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE=1`; in the first-release hook, before Apache starts, it is a note. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html).
13. **smoke test the health endpoint**: skipped when `SQUIRE_SMOKE=0` (Apache is not running inside the first-release hook). Otherwise it requests `SQUIRE_SMOKE_URL` up to `SQUIRE_SMOKE_RETRIES` attempts (default 5), sleeping `SQUIRE_SMOKE_DELAY` seconds (default 2) between them, and fails unless the answer is HTTP 200.

### PROCTOR: the deploy gate [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#proctor-the-deploy-gate)

The release asks PROCTOR's deploy gate, `proctor gate`, for a go or no-go on this commit. The gate runs the deploy-time checks (the PHP floor and runtime, the Laravel line and its PHP range, the lock file, known advisories and the overrides) and ratchets them against a baseline: a failure the running release already had is held, and only a new failure, a first release that fails, or an expired override blocks. The squire holds the gate; the proctor says who may pass.

- **Report or stop.** By default (`SQUIRE_PROCTOR=auto`) a no-go is a warning and the release goes on: a failing post-script cannot undo a Quick Update, because the new commit is already live (S20). With `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce` a no-go stops the release before the frontend build and the migrations: the first release never comes up healthy, and a Quick Update keeps the new commit checked out, so fix the BLOCK lines (or record a dated override in `policy-overrides.json`) and re-run. A gate that could not decide (exit 2) is a warning under `auto` and a stop under `enforce`. `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=skip` skips the step.
- **The record.** Every gated release writes its verdict to `storage/squire/proctor-gate.json` (`SQUIRE_PROCTOR_RECORD_DIR`). When the release goes on (a go, or a reported no-go, which goes live anyway) that verdict is copied to `proctor-gate-baseline.json`, and the next release passes it to the gate as `--baseline`. A stopped release leaves the baseline alone, so re-running after a stop is judged against the release that is really live. The folder gets a `.gitignore` of `*`. The first gated release has no baseline, so every failure blocks it.
- **The runtime.** The gate also grades the PHP that will serve the app for PROCTOR's unpatched check, passed as `--php-runtime` (`SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME`, default `auto`). `auto` asks the php that runs `release.sh`, because that is the one serving the app, and cuts any suffix (`8.4.27-dev` is graded as `8.4.27`); the log says `gate: grading PHP 8.4.27`. An `X.Y.Z` value is graded as given, for a host where the release runs under another php than the web server. `skip` grades no runtime. A value that is not `X.Y.Z` (say `8.4`) or a php that does not answer is a note, and the gate runs without the flag. The older `proctor check` fallback never gets it.
- **An older PROCTOR.** When the installed PROCTOR has no `gate` command, the step prints a warning naming its version, runs `proctor check` as before (a failed check is a report, or a stop under `enforce`), and writes no record. Update `waynestate/proctor` to a release that has the gate.
- The binary is `vendor/bin/proctor`, then `proctor` on PATH, or `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_BIN`. It is a dev dependency, so `--no-dev` removes it: point `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_BIN` at a copy.
- The policy is `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_POLICY` when set; otherwise the policy the CREED package ships (`vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, when installed); otherwise PROCTOR runs on its own default policy with a notice. An explicit value always wins.

### The Oracle check [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#the-oracle-check)

The release also runs an Oracle connection check (`oracle-check.php`) after the migrations and before the smoke test. It is a report, never a gate: a finding prints in the deployment log and the release goes on. When the app does not use Oracle (no `ORACLE_*` settings) it prints nothing. It checks, in order, that the settings are present, that the host resolves, that the port answers within 3 seconds, that the `oci8` driver is loaded, and that the login works, stopping at the first failure so a bad port never costs a login attempt. Settings: `ORACLE_USERNAME`, `ORACLE_PASSWORD`, and either `ORACLE_TNS` (Easy Connect `host:port/service`, or a full `(DESCRIPTION=...)` descriptor) or `ORACLE_HOST`, `ORACLE_PORT` and `ORACLE_SERVICE_NAME`. Only setting names are ever printed, never values.

### Configuration [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#configuration)

Before the first step the script reads two sources: `./.env.squire` (the release options) and the secrets folder, `SQUIRE_SECRETS_DIR` (default `/run/secrets`), where each file named like a variable becomes that variable unless the environment already sets it. Only names are printed. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html#secrets-files-at-run-time-never-in-a-layer).

Configuration is environment variables, all optional, or the same names in `./.env.squire` in the app root. On Citadel add that file as a configuration file (the configuration-files step after the wizard; the wizard has no environment field) and keep it out of git. A variable already in the environment wins over the file. See `.env.squire.example`.

Warning

PROCTOR is a dev dependency and the release installs with `--no-dev`, so `vendor/bin/proctor` is gone by the time the PROCTOR step runs. Set `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_BIN` to a copy that survives, or the step reports itself missing.

### Next [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/release-script.html#next)

Read [Citadel setup](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/citadel-setup.html) for the dashboard steps that make this script run, or [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) to watch the same pipeline on your machine.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html

## Static site [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html#static-site)

For a site with no backend, the squire does double duty: it writes the serving layer and leaves the site itself to you. This page covers `squire init --target=static`, the `SQUIRE_STATIC_ROOT` setting, and the Vue/Inertia layer that sits on top of the target.

### What the static target writes [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html#what-the-static-target-writes)

A static site is a target of its own: `--target=static` writes everything the `raw` target writes, with its own front controller, `public/index.php`, and an `.htaccess` that routes every request that is not a real file to it. The site itself is plain files you commit; the front controller serves them with HELMET's headers, injects the CSP nonce into the HTML, and caches the assets.

### SQUIRE_STATIC_ROOT [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html#squire-static-root)

The site folder is `../../site` by default (the app lives in `deploy/` beside it); point `SQUIRE_STATIC_ROOT` at a different folder. `public/up.php` still answers the health check, because a real file is served straight by Apache and never reaches the front controller.

### The Vue/Inertia layer [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/static-site.html#the-vue-inertia-layer)

A Vue/Inertia app is a layer on `raw`, `laravel` or `static`, not a fourth target: `init` detects `vue` in `package.json` (dependencies or devDependencies) and writes the layer's `.npmrc` and its `docker-compose.squire.yml` (with a Node 22 service) beside the target's files.

- `.npmrc` sets `min-release-age=1` for the frontend install.
- The Vue `docker-compose.squire.yml` is the common parity compose plus a Node 22 service for frontend tooling, pinned to the same major as the Citadel image.

Every app, Vue or not, gets the one common `scripts/release.sh`, which installs the frontend from the lock file and runs the `build` script whenever there is a `package.json`.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html

## Theming your docs [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#theming-your-docs)

A squire swaps the livery without touching the armor: this page shows how to point the docs builder at your own CSS and header. Read [Building the docs](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docs-builder.html) first if you have not met the builder, then add the two files below.

Note

The `theme` key is on a branch and not in a release yet. It is coming in the next release.

### The theme key [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#the-theme-key)

Add a `theme` key to `docs/docs.json` with two paths, `css` and `header`. Both paths are relative to the folder that holds `docs.json`.

```json
{
    "theme": {
        "css": "theme/docs.css",
        "header": "theme/header.html"
    }
}
```

### What the builder does [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#what-the-builder-does)

The builder copies your CSS file to `site/docs/theme/`. Dark mode, fonts and colors live in that theme CSS, and the kit's `docs.css` is never edited.

### Placeholders and links [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#placeholders-and-links)

The header file takes exactly two placeholders, `{{project}}` and `{{version}}`. Any other placeholder fails the build with exit 2. Write header links relative to `site/`, not relative to `docs/`.

The front page can carry the same version. Put `data-docs-version` on the element that holds it, in any top-level `site/*.html` page, and leave only the version text inside: `<span class="brand__version" data-docs-version>0.6.0</span>`. A plain build writes the docs stamp there, and `--check` reports the page stale after a release until you rebuild. Words around the number (Rev, Sheet, v) stay outside the element.

### Checklist [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#checklist)

- [ ] `docs/docs.json` has a `theme` key with `css` and `header`.
- [ ] Both paths are relative to the folder that holds `docs.json`.
- [ ] Your CSS carries dark mode, fonts and colors, and the kit's `docs.css` stays untouched.
- [ ] The header uses only `{{project}}` and `{{version}}`.
- [ ] Header links are relative to `site/`.
- [ ] The front page's version chip carries `data-docs-version`, so it matches the docs.

### A worked example [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/theming.html#a-worked-example)

These pages are one. Squire's `docs/docs.json` names `theme/squire.css` and `_header.html`: the header is the front page's masthead, and the CSS maps the front page's canvas, leather and gold onto the kit's `--dk-*` tokens, then adds the luggage tags, the stitched seams and a derived dark set. Read those two files in the repository for a theme that passes the accessibility gate in light and dark.

The rest of the builder is in [Building the docs](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docs-builder.html).

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html

## Update and drift [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#update-and-drift)

This page explains how Squire tracks the files it writes (the `.squire.json` SHA-256 record), how `init --check` reports drift, how `squire update` moves your copies forward, and how Sourdough keeps its copy of the templates in step. Next, read [Commands](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html) for the full flag reference.

### The `.squire.json` record [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#the-squire-json-record)

`init` records a SHA-256 of each file it writes in `.squire.json`; commit that file. The record is what lets Squire tell the files you never edited from the ones you did.

### Drift: `init --check` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#drift-init-check)

`squire init --check` reports when your copies have drifted from the templates (depend, do not copy). Drift from the Squire templates is reported as a warning under S9, never as a failure: you may edit your copies. See [Doctor](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html) for the rule.

### `squire update` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#squire-update)

`squire update` takes the new template versions for the files you never edited, writes the template files a newer release added to a group the kit records (recording them in `.squire.json`), and shows a diff for the ones you did. It never overwrites your edits, and it runs the same in CI and on a laptop.

`update` reads the record: a file you never edited takes the new template, a file you edited is left alone and shown as a diff, a file a newer release added to a recorded group is written and recorded, and a file Squire did not write is never touched. A squire polishes the armor; the knight keeps the sword. `--dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing.

```
vendor/bin/squire init   [--path=.] [--target=auto|raw|laravel|static] [--only=release|parity] [--check] [--force]
vendor/bin/squire update [--path=.] [--target=raw|laravel|static] [--only=release|parity] [--dry-run]
```

### App-owned files and `--force` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#app-owned-files-and-force)

`init` never overwrites a file you edited, or a file it did not write, unless you pass `--force`. An app that already has its own `public/index.php` or `public/.htaccess` keeps it: `init` reports the file as `app-owned`, never records or overwrites it (not even with `--force`), and `init --check` does not count it as drift. Delete your copy and run `init` to take Squire's. A front controller Squire wrote is tracked like any other file.

### Sourdough's copy of the templates [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html#sourdough-s-copy-of-the-templates)

Sourdough carries a generated copy of Squire's deploy templates instead of writing its own. The copy began when its apps could not `composer require` Squire from an internal repository (no internal URLs may be committed). Squire is on Packagist now, and Sourdough requires it as a dev dependency and regenerates its copy from the package. Squire owns the templates; the copy is checked in and verified, never hand-edited.

```
php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire            # write the copy
php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire --check    # verify it; exit 1 on drift
```

The copy holds, for each kind (`raw`, `laravel`, `static`) and for the Vue layer (`vue`), the files a new app gets from `squire init`, at their target paths, with each file's mode recorded so executables stay executable. `catalog.json` lists which files each kind and layer installs and where; `manifest.json` records the Squire version and a SHA-256 per file. Refresh the copy when Squire's templates move on, and run `--check` in CI to keep it honest. A squire keeps the armor polished; the copy stays in step.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/

## Overview [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#overview)

Squire is the Citadel kit: the standard `build.sh`, the release script, the health check, and a local setup that runs your app on the real Citadel images, behind a proxy like Citadel's. The next step is [installing it](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html), which takes a minute and ends with a doctor check.

### What it does [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#what-it-does)

- `squire init` writes the scripts a Citadel app needs from templates, for raw PHP, Laravel or a static site, and detects a Vue/Inertia layer from `package.json`, adding the layer's release script and Node 22 parity service. `squire init --check` reports when your copies have drifted from the templates (depend, do not copy). In a directory below the repository root (a `deploy/` layer, say), `init` also keeps the `.gitignore` honest: it appends `/vendor/`, `.env` and `.env.squire` when they are missing, never touches a line the app added, and leaves the repository root's `.gitignore` to the app.
- `squire update` takes the new template versions for the files you never edited, writes the template files a newer release added to a group the kit records (recording them in `.squire.json`), and shows a diff for the ones you did. It never overwrites your edits, and it runs the same in CI and on a laptop.
- `squire doctor` checks an app against the best practices a machine can decide. The lock file, composer audit and MySQL 5.6 checks are owned by PROCTOR; `doctor` hands off to it (S50) instead of repeating them.
- A local setup that runs your app on the Citadel PHP image, behind a proxy like Citadel's, with the same MySQL 5.6.
- Squire's maintainers send platform improvement proposals to the platform team privately. Squire never touches a server.

### Where the code lives [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#where-the-code-lives)

The canonical repository is [git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/squire](https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/squire); clone it over SSH as `git@git.wayne.edu:enterprise-apps/squire.git` or over HTTPS as `https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/squire.git`. Open issues and merge requests there; tags are cut there, by a maintainer, with an approver. GitHub ([waynestate/squire](https://github.com/waynestate/squire)) is a read-only push mirror of it: Packagist reads from it, and nobody pushes to it. Your squire serves one banner, and it flies over git.wayne.edu.

### Its place in the stack [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#its-place-in-the-stack)

Squire is part of WELD, the Wayne State application stack, beside WayneUI (project 0, the interface layer every other project builds on), CREED, PROCTOR, Preflight, SESAME, HELMET, Pinstripe, Sourdough, Booster, Rollcall, Drawbridge and ADVISOR.

> A knight never suits up alone. Your app shouldn't deploy alone either.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html

## Install [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

### Requirements [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

PHP `^8.3`, tested on 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. The package runs on your machine or in CI, not on Citadel; what lands on Citadel is the scripts it wrote.

### Install [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

```
composer require waynestate/squire --dev
vendor/bin/squire init
vendor/bin/squire doctor
```

### Verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

`vendor/bin/squire doctor` checks the app against the best practices a machine can decide. Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` findings (`init --check`: drift; `update`: an edited file still differs from the template; `doctor`: a failed rule), `2` the tool itself could not run.

Next: the [command reference](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

The block below is owned by the docs builder: it lists every command the CLI keeps, with its usage, arguments and options, and is rewritten from the repository on every build.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `squire doctor` | Check an app's Citadel release setup against the Squire rules (S1 to S78). |
| `squire init` | Write the standard Citadel scripts into an app, or report drift with --check. |
| `squire update` | Take new template versions for files Squire wrote that were never edited, add the files a newer release wrote, and show a diff for the edited ones. |

#### `squire doctor` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#squire-doctor)

Check an app's Citadel release setup against the Squire rules (S1 to S78).

Usage: `squire doctor [--path PATH] [--format FORMAT] [--] [<topic>]`

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | no | Optional topic. Use `oracle` to check the Oracle connection settings. |

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--format=VALUE` | Output format: text or json. | `text` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `squire init` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#squire-init)

Write the standard Citadel scripts into an app, or report drift with --check.

Usage: `squire init [--path PATH] [--target TARGET] [--only ONLY] [--check] [--force]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--target=VALUE` | raw, laravel or static (default: the target recorded in .squire.json, else laravel when an artisan file exists; static must be asked for). |  |
| `--only=VALUE` | Comma-separated groups to write: release, parity. (default: the groups recorded in .squire.json, else release, parity) |  |
| `--check` | Write nothing; report files that are missing, outdated or edited. Exit 1 on drift. |  |
| `--force` | Overwrite files that were edited or that Squire did not write. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `squire update` [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#squire-update)

Take new template versions for files Squire wrote that were never edited, add the files a newer release wrote, and show a diff for the edited ones.

Usage: `squire update [--path PATH] [--target TARGET] [--only ONLY] [--dry-run]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--path=VALUE` | Path to the application. | `.` |
| `--target=VALUE` | raw, laravel or static (default: the target recorded in .squire.json). |  |
| `--only=VALUE` | Comma-separated groups to update: release, parity. (default: the groups recorded in .squire.json) |  |
| `--dry-run` | Print the plan; write nothing. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

### Exit codes [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

`0` pass, `1` findings (`init --check`: drift; `update`: an edited file still differs from the template; `doctor`: a failed rule), `2` the tool itself could not run.

### doctor oracle [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#doctor-oracle)

`vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle` runs the same plain-language Oracle connection check that `release.sh` runs on Citadel, from your terminal or `sail php vendor/bin/squire doctor oracle`. It reads the `ORACLE_*` settings from the environment and the app's `.env`, prints setting names and never values, and stays silent when the app has no Oracle settings. Add `-v` for the client version.
