Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html

## Configuration reference [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration-reference)

Every `SQUIRE_*` setting Squire reads, grouped by the script that reads it, with the file each group lives in and its default. All settings are optional. Next, see [Commands](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html) for the CLI flags and [Files](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html) for what Squire writes.

Warning

A real environment variable wins. `release.sh` reads the release options from the file, but a variable already in the environment wins. Locally, the same file holds the parity settings.

### Where the settings live [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#where-the-settings-live)

All optional. On Citadel, add `./.env.squire` as a configuration file (the configuration-files step after the wizard; the wizard has no environment field) and keep it out of git. `release.sh` reads the release options from it, and a variable already in the environment wins. Locally, the same file holds the parity settings.

| Group | Reader | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release script | `scripts/release.sh` | `./.env.squire` (on Citadel, added as a configuration file and kept out of git) |
| Front controller | raw `public/index.php`, static `public/index.php` | the app's environment |
| Health check | `health.php` | the app's environment |
| Local parity | the parity compose file | `.env.squire` (see `.env.squire.example`; it holds placeholders only) |
| Portable image | `.squire/portable/squire-entrypoint.sh`, `docker build` | the container's environment, and build arguments |

### Release script (`scripts/release.sh`) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#release-script-scripts-release-sh)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_APP_DIR` | parent of `scripts/` | App root. |
| `SQUIRE_FRAMEWORK` | `auto` | `auto`, `laravel` or `raw`. Laravel is detected from `artisan`. |
| `SQUIRE_ALLOW_ROOT` | `0` | `1` allows running as root. |
| `SQUIRE_REQUIRE_ENV` | `auto` | `1` requires a `.env` file; `auto` means Laravel does. |
| `SQUIRE_WRITABLE_DIRS` | Laravel: `storage`, `bootstrap/cache` | Directories to create. |
| `SQUIRE_COMPOSER_AUDIT` | `report` | `report`, `fail` or `skip`. |
| `SQUIRE_NPM` | `auto` | `auto` or `skip` (for committed built assets). |
| `SQUIRE_NPM_IGNORE_SCRIPTS` | `1` | Install with `--ignore-scripts`. |
| `SQUIRE_NPM_REBUILD` | empty | Packages, separated by spaces, whose install scripts run after the install (`npm rebuild --ignore-scripts=false`, or `pnpm rebuild`; pnpm 10 also needs them in `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies`). The escape hatch for a package that needs its own scripts, such as a native addon. |
| `SQUIRE_NPM_BUILD_SCRIPT` | `build` | The `package.json` script to run. |
| `SQUIRE_CACHE_DIR` | `.cache/squire` | Where Composer and npm keep their download caches between releases, inside the app folder so a Citadel Update keeps them; `off` leaves their defaults. |
| `SQUIRE_MIGRATE` | `1` | Laravel: `migrate --force`. |
| `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE` | `1` | Laravel: `optimize`. |
| `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART` | `1` | Laravel: tell queue workers and `schedule:work` to restart on the new code (`reload`, or `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt`). Report only. |
| `SQUIRE_PROCTOR` | `auto` | `auto`, `skip` or `enforce`. The release asks `proctor gate` for a go or no-go (`proctor check` on a PROCTOR without the gate). By default a no-go is a report and never stops the release; `enforce` makes a no-go stop it, before the frontend build and the migrations. |
| `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_BIN` | `vendor/bin/proctor`, then `PATH` | Where PROCTOR is. It is a dev dependency, so `--no-dev` removes it: point this at a copy. |
| `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_POLICY` | `vendor/waynestate/creed/policy/policy.json`, when installed | Path to the policy file. When unset, the script falls back to the policy the CREED package ships (the deploy wizard has no environment field); when CREED is not installed, PROCTOR runs on its own default policy with a notice. An explicit value always wins. |
| `SQUIRE_PROCTOR_RECORD_DIR` | `storage/squire` | Where the gate keeps its verdicts, relative to the app root: `proctor-gate.json` (the last verdict) and `proctor-gate-baseline.json` (the verdict of the last release that went on, the next run's baseline). The folder gets a `.gitignore` of `*`, so it never reaches git. |
| `SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME` | `auto` | The PHP version the gate grades for PROCTOR's unpatched check, passed as `--php-runtime`: `auto` reads the php that runs `release.sh` (it is the one serving the app; a suffix such as `-dev` is cut), `skip` grades no runtime, and an `X.Y.Z` value is graded as given. A value that is not `X.Y.Z` is a note and grades nothing. Only `proctor gate` gets it; the older `proctor check` fallback does not. |
| `SQUIRE_SMOKE` | `1` | Request the health URL at the end and fail unless it answers 200. |
| `SQUIRE_SMOKE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:80/up` (Laravel), `/up.php` (raw and static) | Full URL. |
| `SQUIRE_SMOKE_RETRIES` | `5` | Attempts. |
| `SQUIRE_SMOKE_DELAY` | `2` | Seconds between attempts. |
| `SQUIRE_SECRETS_DIR` | `/run/secrets` | A folder of secret files, read before the first step: each regular file named like a variable (`DB_PASSWORD`) becomes that variable, unless the environment already sets it. Only names are printed. The fallback entrypoint reads the same folder for Apache. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html). |

### Front controller [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#front-controller)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_APP_ENTRY` | `app.php` | Front controller (raw `public/index.php`): the app's entry, relative to the app directory. |
| `SQUIRE_STATIC_ROOT` | `../../site` | Static `public/index.php`: the site folder. |

### Health check (`health.php`) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#health-check-health-php)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_HEALTH_PATH` | not stated | The path the health check requests. |
| `SQUIRE_HEALTH_PORT` | `80` | The port the health check requests. |
| `SQUIRE_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` | `5`, at most `14`, inside Citadel's `15` | Seconds the health check waits. |
| `SQUIRE_HEALTH_VENDOR` | `1` also requires `vendor/autoload.php` | Whether the health check also requires the autoloader. |
| `SQUIRE_APP_DIR` | the folder `health.php` is in | The app root the check reads (`artisan`, `vendor/`). The portable image sets `/citadel/src`, so a kit in a subfolder checks the app it serves. |

### Portable image (`.squire/portable.Dockerfile`) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#portable-image-squire-portable-dockerfile)

The entrypoint reads these when a container starts; the build arguments are read at `docker build`. Citadel never reads either. See [The portable image](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html).

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_ROLE` | `web` | `web`, `worker`, `scheduler` or `migrate`. A first argument naming a role wins. |
| `SQUIRE_PORT` | `PORT`, else `8080` | The port Apache listens on and the health check asks. Below 1024 is refused for a user that is not root. |
| `PORT` | not set | Read when `SQUIRE_PORT` is not set (the name several platforms set). |
| `SQUIRE_WORKER_COMMAND` | `php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --max-time=3600 --sleep=3` | The worker's command, split on spaces. Required for a raw PHP app. |
| `SQUIRE_SCHEDULER_COMMAND` | `php artisan schedule:work` | The scheduler's command. Required for a raw PHP app. |
| `SQUIRE_MIGRATE_COMMAND` | `php artisan migrate --force` | The migrate role's command; a raw PHP app without one has nothing to migrate. |
| `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE` | `1` | Laravel: `php artisan optimize` when a `web`, `worker` or `scheduler` container starts. |
| `SQUIRE_SECRETS_DIR` | `/run/secrets` | The same secrets loader as the release script, before any role starts. |
| `SQUIRE_KIT_DIR` (build argument) | `.` | Where the kit sits in the build context (`deploy` for WELD). |
| `SQUIRE_WRITABLE_DIRS` (build argument) | Laravel: `storage bootstrap/cache` | Folders handed to group 0 and made group-writable, separated by spaces. |
| `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE` (build argument) | `0` | Baked code: opcache never checks files. A run-time `1` still wins. |
| `SQUIRE_KEEP_NODE_MODULES` (build argument) | `0` | `1` keeps `node_modules/` in the image after the frontend build. By default it is removed in the same step, because no role runs Node. |

### PHP in the image (`.squire/php.ini`) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#php-in-the-image-squire-php-ini)

PHP reads these from the container's environment when it starts (PHP 8.3 and later). The parity compose file passes `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE` and `SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS` from `.env.squire`; on Citadel the platform's own `php.ini` decides. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html).

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE` | `1` | How code arrives. `1`: pulled into the running container (Citadel, a bind mount, or unknown), so opcache checks files every 2 seconds. `0`: baked into an image that never changes, so it never checks. Also a build argument of `.squire/Dockerfile` (default `1`); the run-time value wins. Never empty: that turns the checks off. |
| `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_MEMORY` | `128` | opcache memory, in megabytes. |
| `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_MAX_FILES` | `20000` | How many scripts opcache keeps. |
| `SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS` | `exec,passthru,shell_exec,system,pcntl_exec,phpinfo,show_source,highlight_file` | The web's `disable_functions` list (`.squire/php-web.ini`; the CLI disables nothing). It replaces the list; `none` disables nothing. Leave it unset for the default: an empty value disables nothing too. |

### Local parity (`.env.squire`) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#local-parity-env-squire)

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SQUIRE_PROJECT` | not stated | Local parity: the project name. |
| `SQUIRE_BASE_IMAGE` | not stated | Local parity: the app image. |
| `SQUIRE_PROXY_IMAGE` | not stated | Local parity: the proxy image. |
| `SQUIRE_MYSQL_IMAGE` | not stated | Local parity: the MySQL image. |
| `SQUIRE_PUBLIC_DIR` | not stated | Local parity: the public directory. |
| `SQUIRE_SERVER_NAME` | not stated | Local parity: the server name. |
| `SQUIRE_TZ` | not stated | Local parity: the timezone. |
| `SQUIRE_ENVIRONMENT` | not stated | Local parity: the environment. |
| `SQUIRE_DEPLOYMENTS` | not stated | Local parity: the deployments path. |
| `SQUIRE_HTTP_PORT` | not stated | Local parity: the HTTP port. |
| `SQUIRE_APP_MEMORY` | not stated | Local parity: the app memory limit. |
| `SQUIRE_SOURCE_UID` | not stated | Local parity: the uid that owns the mounted source. |
| `SQUIRE_SOURCE_GID` | not stated | Local parity: the gid that owns the mounted source. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_NAME` | not stated | Local parity: the database name. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_USER` | not stated | Local parity: the database user. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_PASSWORD` | not stated | Local parity: the database password. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | not stated | Local parity: the database root password. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_PORT` | not stated | Local parity: the database port. |
| `SQUIRE_DB_MEMORY` | not stated | Local parity: the database memory limit. |
| `SQUIRE_PORTABLE_HTTP_PORT` | `8081` | The `portable` profile: where the web container is published on loopback. |
| `SQUIRE_PORTABLE_USER` | `10001:0` | The `portable` profile: the UID and group the containers run as (try `1000123:0`). |
| `SQUIRE_PORTABLE_ENV_FILE` | `.env` | The `portable` profile: the app's env file, read at run time and never baked in. |
| `SQUIRE_PORTABLE_CONTEXT` | `.` | The `portable` profile: the build context, relative to the compose file (`..` for WELD). |
| `SQUIRE_KIT_DIR` | `.` | The `portable` profile: the kit's folder inside that context (`deploy` for WELD). |

The Vue layer's compose file also reads `SQUIRE_NODE_IMAGE` (default `node:22.23.4-bookworm-slim`, pinned by digest), `SQUIRE_NODE_ENV` (default `production`) and `SQUIRE_NODE_MEMORY` (default `512m`). The compose file refuses to start without the two passwords. See `.env.squire.example`; it holds placeholders only.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html

## Files Squire writes [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html#files-squire-writes)

What `squire init` writes into your app, which target or layer each file belongs to, and the `.gitignore` lines `init` keeps honest. Next, see [Quick start](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) to write your first set of files and [Configuration](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html) for the settings they read.

### What lands in your app [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html#what-lands-in-your-app)

| File | What it is | Target or layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build.sh` | Citadel's build hook: system packages only, POSIX sh, runs as root with no app source. No Composer, no npm. | All targets |
| `deployments/001-first-release.sh` | Runs once per app: calls the release script with the smoke test off (Apache is not up yet). | All targets |
| `scripts/release.sh` | The idempotent release: preconditions, `composer install --no-dev` from the lock file, audit, PROCTOR's deploy gate (`proctor gate`, a report by default, a stop with `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), frontend build, Laravel `migrate --force` and `optimize`, an Oracle connection check (a report, never a gate), `/up` smoke test. Use it as the Quick Update post-script as well. | All targets |
| `health.php` | Citadel's health check (`["php","health.php"]`): one HTTP request to `/up`, never boots the framework. | All targets |
| `oracle-check.php` | The plain-language Oracle connection check the release runs: settings, host, port, driver, login. A report, never a gate; silent when the app has no `ORACLE_*` settings. | All targets |
| `public/up.php` | The endpoint that answers `ok`. Laravel has `/up` built in. | Raw PHP and static |
| `public/index.php` | Raw: the front controller that serves `public/` files safely and hands the rest to the app's entry. Static: the one that serves the committed site with HELMET's headers. Never written over an app's own. | Raw and static |
| `public/.htaccess` | Raw: sends every request but `index.php` and `up.php` to the front controller. Static: routes every request that is not a real file to it. | Raw and static |
| `.npmrc` | Sets `min-release-age=1` (days) for the frontend install, with the escape hatches in its comments. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html#npm-no-install-scripts-no-day-old-versions). | Vue layer only |
| `docker-compose.squire.yml` | The common parity compose plus a Node 22 service for frontend tooling. | Vue layer only |
| `docker-compose.squire.yml`, `.squire/`, `.env.squire.example`, `scripts/parity.sh`, `scripts/parity.ps1` | Local parity. | Local parity kit |
| `.squire/apache-hardening.conf` | `ServerTokens Prod`, `ServerSignature Off` and `TraceEnable Off`, enabled by the fallback base. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html). | Local parity kit |
| `.squire/portable.Dockerfile`, `.squire/portable.Dockerfile.dockerignore` | The portable image for platforms other than Citadel: the code baked in, `USER 10001:0`, group-0 writable folders, port 8080, `STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM`. Its ignore file keeps `.env`, secrets, `.git`, `vendor/` and `node_modules/` out of the build. See [The portable image](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/portable-image.html). | Local parity kit |
| `.squire/portable/squire-entrypoint.sh` | The portable image's entrypoint: the `web`, `worker`, `scheduler`, `migrate` and `health` roles, picked by argument or `SQUIRE_ROLE`. | Local parity kit |
| `.squire/portable/ports.conf`, `.squire/portable/vhost.conf` | Apache for the portable image: `Listen ${SQUIRE_PORT}`, the same document root as Citadel's vhost, logs to stdout and stderr. | Local parity kit |
| `.squire/php-web.ini` | The web's own settings: the `disable_functions` list. The app image appends it to `php.ini` as `php-apache2handler.ini`, so the CLI keeps every function. See [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html). | Local parity kit |

### The .gitignore lines init keeps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html#the-gitignore-lines-init-keeps)

In a directory below the repository root (a `deploy/` layer, say), `init` also keeps the `.gitignore` honest: it appends `/vendor/`, `.env` and `.env.squire` when they are missing, never touches a line the app added, and leaves the repository root's `.gitignore` to the app.

### Conventions [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/files.html#conventions)

Every shell script uses `set -euo pipefail` (`build.sh` uses `set -eu`, because Citadel runs it with `/bin/sh`), prints a `[squire] ==> step N: ...` marker for each step, and can be run twice with the same result.

Note

`init` records a SHA-256 of each file in `.squire.json`; commit that file. `init --check` reports when your copies have drifted from the templates (depend, do not copy), and `update` takes the new template versions for the files you never edited.

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html

## Proof [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page says how Squire was proven on real Wayne State applications: what ran, what held, what the run caught in Squire itself, and what it does not prove yet. Next, see [Doctor](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html) for the rules the run checked and [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) for the setup the boots used.

A squire is judged on the field, not in the tent. So on 2026-11-05 Squire went out to every PHP application in the stack's shared proof corpus, the same set PROCTOR and Preflight are measured on.

### Last run [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#last-run)

The table below records the most recent time the checks on this page were run against Squire itself, so a reader can see when the page was last verified and what the run found.

| Check | Date | Commit | Result | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composer ci` | 2026-11-07 | 88fd2ec | pass: 404 tests, 2771 assertions, 0 phpstan errors, 0 advisories | 8m 14s |
| Local parity rig (`parity.sh up --fallback`, shell twin under WSL 2 bash) | 2026-11-07 | 88fd2ec | pass: the release ran all eight steps in 6s and `/up.php` answered 200 with body `ok` through the proxy | 27s to healthy (images prebuilt on this machine) |

To refresh this section, rerun `composer ci` and the local parity rig from [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html), then rewrite the table. The 82-app corpus run and the four real-app boots were not rerun: they need the shared proof corpus and the internal app repositories, which are not available on this machine, so the parity row uses the synthetic fixture that `squire init` writes, the same way CI does.

### What ran [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-ran)

Squire 0.5.0 from `main`, plus the `init` notice described below, in `php:8.4-cli` with no network. The 82 applications are 64 raw PHP apps (33 with a `composer.json`, 31 without one), 17 Laravel apps from 5.8 to 13, and 1 Slim 2 app. Six libraries, one template and six test sites ran too and are counted on their own line.

Each app was a throwaway copy of its default branch, checked out with Linux line endings, with `.env` files, `auth.json` and `config.files/` removed, and made into a fresh git repository so `doctor` could see what is tracked. Then, in order:

1. `squire doctor --format=json` on the app as it was;
2. `squire init`, letting Squire pick the target;
3. `squire init --check`, which must find no drift in what `init` just wrote;
4. `squire init` again, which must change nothing;
5. `squire doctor --format=json` on the result;
6. `squire update --dry-run`;
7. a lint of every file `init` wrote: `sh -n` or `bash -n` for the shell scripts, `php -l` for the PHP, a JSON parse for `.squire.json`, and a search for carriage returns.

An app **passes** when every step does what it should and `doctor` ends with exit 0. It is **flagged** when Squire did its job and still has something to tell the app (a fail or an untracked file the app wrote itself). A **tool error** is Squire breaking: a crash, an exit 2, invalid JSON, drift in its own output, a second `init` that changes something, or a written file that fails its lint.

### Results [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#results)

| Units | Pass | Flagged | Tool error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 82 applications | 76 | 6 | 0 |
| 13 libraries, template and test sites | 10 | 3 | 0 |

| Shape | Apps | Target `init` picked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw PHP, no `composer.json` | 31 | raw |
| Raw PHP with Composer | 33 | raw |
| Slim 2 | 1 | raw |
| Laravel 5.8 to 13 | 17 | laravel (from `artisan`) |

- `init` wrote 18 to 21 files per app, and every one of them passed its lint. A second `init` changed nothing anywhere.
- 36 apps already had their own `public/index.php` and 2 their own `public/.htaccess`. `init` reported each as `app-owned` and left it alone, as documented.
- The six flagged apps had their own `build.sh` or `health.php`. `init` skipped those files without `--force`, `init --check` named them as untracked, and in one of them `doctor` failed S1: its own `build.sh` runs `composer require`, which cannot work at image build time.
- The median app took 3 seconds for all seven steps.

### Four apps on local parity [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#four-apps-on-local-parity)

Doctor reads files; it never runs an app. To see whether the kit actually brings an app up, four apps of different shapes were booted on [local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) with the fallback base image, HAProxy in front and MySQL 5.6.51 behind, with every Wayne State host mapped to `127.0.0.1` so no app could reach a real service.

| App shape | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Raw PHP, no `composer.json` | The first release stopped at step 1: `composer.json not found`. See below. |
| Raw PHP with Composer | Healthy in 23 seconds. `/up.php` answered `ok` through the proxy. The app's own front page answered 500 without its configuration, which the proof does not supply. |
| Slim 2 | The release stopped at step 3: the lock file installs one package from Subversion, and the image has no `svn`. The message named the step and the cause. |
| Laravel 13 | Without a `.env`, step 1 refused, as documented. With one made from `.env.example`, as the Citadel dashboard would, the release ran all ten steps in 106 seconds, including the migrations on MySQL 5.6. The app's own `.htaccess` then redirects every plain HTTP request to HTTPS, so `/up` answered 307 and the health check said unhealthy. That is the trusted-proxy class of problem parity exists to show before Citadel does. |

### What it caught in Squire [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-it-caught-in-squire)

A run that only finds praise was not looking hard enough. This one found these, and every finding is about Squire, not the apps:

- **Fixed: the release needs a lock file, and `init` never said so.** 31 of the 82 apps have no `composer.json` and no `composer.lock`. `init` wrote a release into each, `doctor` passed it, and the first boot showed that release stopping at step 1. `init` now ends with a "Heads up" line naming the missing files and how to make them; see [Troubleshooting](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html).
- **Open: Yarn.** Two apps keep a `yarn.lock`. The release installs JavaScript only from `package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so step 5 stops with "commit a lock file", which reads oddly when one is committed. `SQUIRE_NPM=skip` works around it when the built assets are committed.
- **Open: fresh output that warns about itself.** Right after `init`, `doctor` warns on every app that `.env.squire` is not ignored at the repository root (`init` only edits `.gitignore` in a folder below the root) and that the Citadel image in the compose file is not pinned by digest (S67). Both warnings are true and both have a documented fix, but a kit should not hand its owner homework on day one.
- **Windows checkouts.** The first pass used clones made on Windows, where Git had turned the line endings of existing deploy scripts into CRLF. `doctor` failed S8 on 11 apps that are LF in their repositories, exactly the trap the rule describes. The numbers above are from the Linux checkout Citadel sees.

### What this does not prove [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#what-this-does-not-prove)

- No app was deployed to Citadel and no Quick Update ran. The boots used the fallback base image, an approximation of Citadel's image, and only four apps were booted.
- No real configuration, database contents, Oracle, CAS or Entra were used, so an app's own pages are only shown to start, not to work.
- `doctor` decides only the rules a machine can read from files; the rest of the best practices are not checked here.
- The per-app record names the applications and stays in the stack's internal notes.

### Run it on your app [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#run-it-on-your-app)

The same steps on your own app, from its root:

```sh
composer require waynestate/squire --dev
vendor/bin/squire doctor
vendor/bin/squire init
vendor/bin/squire init --check
vendor/bin/squire doctor
```

Then bring it up on local parity:

Linux / macOS

```sh
scripts/parity.sh up --fallback
```

Windows

```powershell
scripts\parity.ps1 up -Fallback
```

## Troubleshooting [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

Symptoms you may meet setting up a Squire app, each with its cause, a fix and a check command. Only what the README and the open questions ground is listed here. Next, see [Doctor](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/doctor.html) for the full rule list and [Local parity](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/local-parity.html) for the parity setup.

### Symptoms [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#symptoms)

#### The first release stops at step 1: composer.json not found [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-first-release-stops-at-step-1-composer-json-not-found)

Cause: `scripts/release.sh` installs from the lock file, so it requires `composer.json` and `composer.lock` in the app root and stops at step 1 (check preconditions) without them. A raw PHP app that never used Composer has neither. `squire init` prints a "Heads up" line when it writes the release into such an app.

Fix: give the app the two files, even with no dependencies, and commit both: `composer init` writes `composer.json`, then `composer update` writes `composer.lock`.

Check:

```sh
ls composer.json composer.lock
vendor/bin/squire init --check
```

#### Permission error writing vendor/ [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#permission-error-writing-vendor)

Cause: on the first end-to-end run, the release hook failed with `Permission denied` writing `vendor/composer/installed.json` because the source folder (created on the host by another tool, owned by root) was not writable by the container's `citadel` user (OPEN_QUESTIONS 15). If the build step fails with a permission error writing `vendor/`, the source folder is not writable by the container's `citadel` user (uid 1000 by default).

Fix: on Linux set `SQUIRE_SOURCE_UID` and `SQUIRE_SOURCE_GID` to yours. After making it writable the hook ran, the app became healthy and the proxy answered. Not solved for Docker Desktop folders that are root-owned.

Check:

```sh
ls -ld <your-source-folder>
scripts/parity.sh status
```

#### uid or gid mismatch between host and container [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#uid-or-gid-mismatch-between-host-and-container)

Cause: the parity container runs as the `citadel` user, uid 1000 by default. When your host user does not match, the mounted source is not writable and the release hook fails with `Permission denied` (OPEN_QUESTIONS 15).

Fix: set `SQUIRE_SOURCE_UID` and `SQUIRE_SOURCE_GID` in `.env.squire` to your host uid and gid, then bring the stack back up.

Check:

```sh
id -u
id -g
scripts/parity.sh status
```

#### init refuses to overwrite a file [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#init-refuses-to-overwrite-a-file)

Cause: `init` never overwrites a file you edited, or a file it did not write, unless you pass `--force`. An app-owned `public/index.php` or `public/.htaccess` is reported as `app-owned`, never recorded or overwritten (not even with `--force`).

Fix: delete your copy and run `init` to take Squire's, or pass `--force` for a file Squire wrote.

Check:

```sh
vendor/bin/squire init --check
```

#### doctor exit codes [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#doctor-exit-codes)

Cause: `doctor` ends with `0` pass, `1` findings (a failed rule), `2` the tool itself could not run.

Fix: for `1`, read the findings and fix the failed rules. For `2`, the tool could not run at all, so check your PHP setup before anything else.

Check:

```sh
vendor/bin/squire doctor --format=json
echo $?
```

#### Bind mounts on Windows [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#bind-mounts-on-windows)

Cause: bind mounts from the Windows side are much slower (Composer and npm installs feel it most), and file ownership and permissions do not map cleanly; that is the cause of the `Permission denied` failure described under the bind-mount question (OPEN_QUESTIONS 15).

Fix: keep the app's source tree inside the WSL 2 Linux filesystem (for example under `~/src` in your WSL distribution) and run `scripts/parity.sh` from there, not from a Windows folder such as `C:\Users\you\...` reached through `/mnt/c`. Advice, not a requirement. The PowerShell `scripts\parity.ps1` still works from a Windows folder, only slower.

Check:

```sh
scripts/parity.sh status
```

#### No access to the real image [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#no-access-to-the-real-image)

Cause: the real Citadel image is internal and has no pullable digest to pin (OPEN_QUESTIONS 19 and the missing configuration list).

Fix: `--fallback` builds an approximation from the official `php` image plus Citadel's extensions. It is good for trying Squire out and not for proving parity.

Check:

```sh
scripts/parity.sh up --fallback
```

#### Scripts lose their executable bit on Windows [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#scripts-lose-their-executable-bit-on-windows)

Cause: Git on Windows does not keep the executable bit (OPEN_QUESTIONS 11).

Fix: mark the scripts executable in git.

```sh
git update-index --chmod=+x build.sh scripts/*.sh deployments/*.sh
```

Check:

```sh
git ls-files -s build.sh scripts/*.sh deployments/*.sh
```

#### Parity compose refuses to start [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#parity-compose-refuses-to-start)

Cause: `.env.squire.example` holds `change-me-local-only` placeholders, and the compose file refuses to start without the two passwords.

Fix: copy the example to `.env.squire` and set the passwords.

```sh
cp .env.squire.example .env.squire
```

Check:

```sh
scripts/parity.sh status
```

#### A full Update does not refresh vendor/ [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-full-update-does-not-refresh-vendor)

Cause: deployment hooks run once per app lifetime, so a changed `composer.lock` on a full Update has no install step (OPEN_QUESTIONS 2).

Fix: tell teams to also use `scripts/release.sh` as the Quick Update post-script. Needs a Citadel maintainer's answer.

Check:

```sh
vendor/bin/squire doctor
```

---

Source: https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html

## Upgrading [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

A squire keeps the armor a season ahead: this page walks each released minor of Squire, newest first, with what changed, the steps to take, and how to verify the upgrade held. It states only what the CHANGELOG states (the full record is in [Changelog](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)); after you move a version, run the two checks below and read [Update and drift](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/update-and-drift.html) for what they report.

### The two checks [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#the-two-checks)

The same two checks verify every upgrade on this page, from the app root:

vendor/bin/squire init --check vendor/bin/squire update --dry-run

`squire init --check` reports when your copies have drifted from the templates; it exits `0` when they match and `1` when they have. `squire update --dry-run` prints the plan and writes nothing; it exits `1` when an edited file still differs from the template. Exit `2` means the tool itself could not run. For the full command reference, see [Commands](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html).

### 0.10.2 (2026-11-09) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-10-2-2026-11-09)

No breaks for an app that builds with Docker: a patch on 0.10.1. Three kit files change. Raw PHP apps get SameSite=Lax session cookies: the kit's `php.ini` sets `session.cookie_samesite = Lax` (it was empty), next to the `session.cookie_httponly = 1` and `session.cookie_secure = 1` it already set, so an app that never calls `helmet_boot()` sends a session cookie SESAME has nothing to warn about (wherever the kit's `php.ini` is used: local parity and the portable image; on Citadel the platform's `php.ini` decides). The kit's Dockerfiles name every image in full (`docker.io/library/php:...`), so Buildah and Podman build them with short-name mode enforcing, and the fallback base takes its Composer image as a build argument (`COMPOSER_IMAGE`) like PHP and Node. The portable image drops `node_modules/` after the frontend build.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer update waynestate/squire` when the app already requires `^0.10`, otherwise `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.10.2`.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new `.squire/php.ini`, `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` and `.squire/portable.Dockerfile` when the app never edited them, and shows a diff when it did.
3. Commit the changed kit files and `.squire.json`.
4. A CI job that builds the fallback base through a pull-through proxy and prefixes the `ARG` defaults itself: the defaults now start with `docker.io/library/`, so strip that before adding the proxy prefix, and pass `COMPOSER_IMAGE` the same way instead of rewriting `COPY --from` (the loop is in [Image hardening](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-hardening.html#through-a-proxy-or-a-mirror)). A job that passes no build arguments needs no change.
5. An app whose session must survive a cross-site POST (a form another site posts to, or a SAML ACS that reads the session on the POST itself) sets `session.cookie_samesite` back for that app, or parks the POST and finishes on a GET the way SESAME's SAML driver does. A CAS ticket and an OIDC code come back on a top-level GET, which still carries a Lax cookie.
6. Stack repos: refresh `deploy/` the same way. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify)

Run the two checks at the top of this page; both exit `0`. `.squire/php.ini` sets `session.cookie_samesite = Lax`, `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` has an `ARG COMPOSER_IMAGE=docker.io/library/composer:2.11.1@sha256:...` line, and a built portable image has no `/citadel/src/node_modules`.

### 0.10.1 (2026-11-09) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-10-1-2026-11-09)

No breaks: a patch on 0.10.0. The kit's fallback base (`.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile`) moves Composer from 2.10.3 to 2.11.1. 2.10 is no longer maintained, and 2.11.0 fixed GHSA-c968-33g3-wh7p (package names in `installed.json` could escape the vendor directory) and GHSA-fm2w-xgf2-f9fh (inline repository HTTP headers could be written into `composer.lock`). 2.11 drops the `source-fallback` setting, which Squire never used, and its new `policy.cooldown` stays off by default. The other two changes are Squire's own: its `deploy/` copy is on the 0.10.0 kit, and `scripts/a11y.ps1` works on a Windows checkout with CRLF line endings.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-1)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer update waynestate/squire` when the app already requires `^0.10`, otherwise `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.10.1`.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` when the app never edited it, and shows a diff when it did.
3. Commit the changed kit files (`.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` and `.squire.json`). The fallback image takes the new Composer the next time it builds.
4. Stack repos: refresh `deploy/` the same way. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-1)

Run the two checks at the top of this page; both exit `0`. `.squire/base-fallback.Dockerfile` names `composer:2.11.1`.

### 0.10.0 (2026-11-09) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-10-0-2026-11-09)

No breaks, and no kit file changes: an app that takes 0.10.0 gets the same files as 0.9.0. The release adds the MySQL upgrade path guide ([MySQL upgrade path](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/mysql-upgrade-path.html)) with a read-only pre-upgrade check script, and docs kit fixes for sites built with Squire's docs builder: the heading "#" stays on the line of its last word, and "On this page" marks the section in view. A site takes those by resyncing the kit and builder with `--sync-to` (see [Docs builder](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docs-builder.html)).

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-2)

2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`; it records the new release in `.squire.json`.

### 0.9.0 (2026-11-08) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-9-0-2026-11-08)

One behavior change for Laravel apps: the release script now checks the app's environment before anything installs. A release stops when `APP_KEY` is unset, or when `APP_DEBUG` is true in production, and an `APP_ENV` that is not `production` earns a warning (Sourdough practice 4.14). The release gate also passes `--php-runtime` to PROCTOR, so the deploy path grades the PHP that serves the app for PROCTOR's unpatched check; `SQUIRE_PHP_RUNTIME` (`auto` by default, `skip`, or an `X.Y.Z` version) changes what it grades.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-3)

1. Before you deploy, make sure the Citadel environment sets `APP_KEY` (in `.env` or as a masked variable in the Citadel dashboard) and sets `APP_DEBUG` to false.
2. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.9`.
3. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new `scripts/release.sh` and `.env.squire.example` when the app never edited them, and shows a diff when it did.
4. Stack repos: refresh `deploy/` the same way. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-3)

Run the two checks at the top of this page; both exit `0`. `scripts/release.sh` checks `APP_KEY` and `APP_DEBUG` (search it for `Sourdough practice 4.14`).

### 0.8.0 (2026-11-08) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-8-0-2026-11-08)

No breaks. The portable image (`.squire/portable.Dockerfile`, ADR-0010) bakes the code in and runs as `web`, `worker`, `scheduler` or `migrate`, picked by argument or `SQUIRE_ROLE`, as a non-root user in group 0 with Apache on 8080, for OpenShift, Coolify and raw Docker. `health.php` reads `SQUIRE_APP_DIR` for the app root, so a kit kept in a subfolder checks the app it serves. The release script keeps Composer's and npm's download caches in `.cache/squire` inside the app folder, so a Citadel Update no longer downloads every package again. The Citadel path is unchanged.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-4)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.8`.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it adds the portable files and shows a diff for any kit file the app edited.
3. Stack repos: refresh `deploy/` the same way. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-4)

Run the two checks at the top of this page; both exit `0`. The app now carries the five new portable files, led by `.squire/portable.Dockerfile`.

### 0.7.1 (2026-11-08) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-7-1-2026-11-08)

No breaks: a patch on 0.7.0. The kit's `php.ini` no longer sets `session.sid_length` or `session.sid_bits_per_character`. PHP 8.4 deprecated both and raises a notice for each, and leaving them out gives PHP's default session ID (32 hex characters, 128 bits), which is what HELMET and SESAME's S45 expect. Squire's own `deploy/.squire.json` also records the `release.sh` it ships, so `squire update` on Squire itself no longer refuses that file.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-5)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.7.1`.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new `.squire/php.ini` when the app never edited it, and shows a diff when it did. Keep your edits and drop the two `session.sid_` lines.
3. Stack repos: refresh `deploy/` the same way. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-5)

Run the two checks at the top of this page; both exit `0`. `.squire/php.ini` has no `session.sid_length` or `session.sid_bits_per_character` line.

### 0.7.0 (2026-11-08) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-7-0-2026-11-08)

#### Breaking [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking)

One behavior change for the web: the app image now sets `disable_functions` for mod_php to `exec`, `passthru`, `shell_exec`, `system`, `pcntl_exec`, `phpinfo`, `show_source` and `highlight_file`. Web code that calls one of them stops working. The CLI (Composer scripts, artisan, the health check, the release script) keeps every function, and `proc_open` and `popen` stay for Symfony Mailer, Laravel's Process and PHPMailer. An app that needs one back sets `SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS` to its own list, or to `none`. The kit's `php.ini` also stops setting `disable_classes`, which PHP 8.5 removed.

#### What changed [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-changed)

**Hardening.** The fallback base sets `ServerTokens Prod`, `ServerSignature Off` and `TraceEnable Off`. The kit's `php.ini` turns on production opcache for the web, with one switch, `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE`: `1` (the default) checks files every 2 seconds, for code pulled into a running container such as a Citadel Quick Update; `0` never checks, for an image that bakes its code in. The release script and the fallback entrypoint load secrets mounted as files from `SQUIRE_SECRETS_DIR` (default `/run/secrets`). `SQUIRE_NPM_REBUILD` lets named packages run their install scripts after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Every image the kit pulls is pinned by its multi-arch list digest. The image contract suite checks the hardening inside the running image.

**Release script.** After `laravel optimize`, a new report-only step restarts Laravel's long-lived processes: `php artisan reload` where Laravel has it, otherwise `queue:restart` and `schedule:interrupt`, each only when that command exists. `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_RESTART=0` turns it off (WELD W22). A new "check opcache" step never fails.

**Fixed.** `squire update` records the current release in `.squire.json` even when every file already matches it. The pipeline's PROCTOR jobs no longer pass `--policy`. The docs kit's copy button and mobile menu, and the front page's quick start and Get started prompt, are fixed (see the CHANGELOG).

**CI and deploy layer.** CI pins the Preflight components to 0.3.1 and runs its a11y component on `site/`, blocking. Squire's own deploy layer requires HELMET `^1.0` and PROCTOR `^0.8`.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-6)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency: `composer require --dev waynestate/squire:^0.7`.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new template versions for the files you never edited and shows a diff for the ones you did.
3. If web code calls one of the disabled functions, set `SQUIRE_PHP_DISABLE_FUNCTIONS` in the app's environment (see [Configuration](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html)) or move that call to a command.
4. An app that bakes its code into the image (OpenShift, Coolify, raw Docker) sets `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE=0`. Citadel apps keep the default.
5. Stack repos: regenerate the `deploy/` folder with `squire init` and check it with `squire init --check`. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire` and verify it with `--check`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-6)

Run `squire init --check` and `squire update --dry-run` (the two checks at the top of this page); both exit `0` once the kit is at the new release. After the next release on the server, the release log shows the "laravel restart long-lived processes" and "check opcache" steps.

### 0.6.0 (2026-11-07) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-6-0-2026-11-07)

#### Breaking [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-1)

None: the CHANGELOG records no breaking change for 0.6.0.

#### What changed [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-changed-1)

**Fixed.** `squire update` writes the template files a newer release added to a group the kit records: a file the target release has that `.squire.json` does not list is written from the template, recorded, and printed as added, so one `update` converges the kit instead of leaving the new files to `squire init`. A file the app already has is still left alone, and an edited file is still refused and shown as a diff. `squire init` without `--only` defaults to the groups the `.squire.json` records instead of `release,parity`, so a bare `init` completes an existing kit without dropping its groups; with no manifest it still writes `release,parity`, and `--only` still wins.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-7)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency to the next release.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update`: it takes the new template versions for the files you never edited, writes the files the release added, and shows a diff for the ones you did.
3. Stack repos: regenerate the `deploy/` folder with `squire init` and check it with `squire init --check`. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire` and verify it with `--check`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-7)

Run `squire init --check` and `squire update --dry-run` (the two checks at the top of this page); both exit `0` once the kit is at the new release.

### 0.5.0 (2026-11-03) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-5-0-2026-11-03)

#### Breaking [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-2)

None: the CHANGELOG records no breaking change for 0.5.0.

#### What changed [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-changed-2)

**New.** An ADVISOR module (`waynestate/advisor`) with `squire_doctor` and `squire_drift`, so a coding agent that runs ADVISOR can run Squire's checks without leaving its sandbox (see [ADVISOR](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/advisor.html)). `squire doctor oracle` runs the Oracle connection check on demand, reading `ORACLE_*` settings from the environment and `.env`. CI publishes the multi-arch Oracle images to the project's container registry when a version is tagged. `scripts/contract-image.sh` runs `release.sh` inside the fallback image and asserts the smoke URL, `health.php` and the first-release log. `bin/docs-site.php`, the shared docs builder, with the kit's `docs.css` and `docs.js`; it turns `docs/` into a committed, WayneUI-styled `site/docs/` and fails CI when the pages are stale or a finding is present (see [The docs builder](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/docs-builder.html)). The docs builder renders a Source link in the header and footer, with a Mirrors list beside it, from the optional `source` and `mirrors` keys in `docs/nav.json`; a source or mirror URL that is not https is a finding. The docs builder's generated blocks: `docs/docs.json` defines blocks that own marked regions in `docs/**/*.md`; the `json-table` type renders a Markdown table from a command's JSON output, the `symfony-commands` type runs `<run> list --format=json` and renders the command reference, and the `env` type scans the scan folders for prefixed environment variable names and renders them with describe meanings and defaults; `--check` reports a stale block instead of writing.

**CI.** GitHub CI now pins the Preflight reusable workflow to the 0.1.3 tag instead of a commit SHA. CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's `CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX`), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit. A `contract-image` job on GitHub runs `scripts/contract-image.sh` on amd64 and arm64. `contract-parity-sh` and `contract-parity-pwsh` jobs on GitHub bring the local parity stack up on the fallback image and check the proxy answers. A front page accessibility gate (`tools/a11y`: axe-core in Playwright, WCAG 2.2 AA) with `scripts/a11y.sh` and `scripts/a11y.ps1` that run it in Docker; GitHub gets an `a11y` job, continue-on-error until it has been seen green once. The PROCTOR deploy job is blocking now.

**Changed.** The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.4.0 (the Oracle check script and the updated build and release scripts). The Oracle image recipes use fully qualified `COPY --from` names so buildah can resolve them; the CI dry run shows amd64 builds need qemu binfmt on the runner (see OPEN_QUESTIONS). The docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

**Fixed.** The fallback base image builds when the host's uid or gid already exists in the image (GitHub runners use 1001). The PowerShell parity script passes the host's uid and gid to the fallback base image build (1000 on Windows, the current user's ids on Linux and macOS) instead of hard-coded 1000, so the app container starts when the bind-mounted source is owned by another user. The contract-image CI job installs PHP and the Composer dependencies before running `scripts/contract-image.sh`, so it no longer stops on the missing `vendor/autoload.php`. The contract-image job builds with the docker buildx driver so the app image finds the freshly built fallback base. `scripts/a11y.sh` and `scripts/a11y.ps1` create `tools/a11y/node_modules` on the host before `docker run`, so the named volume's mount point exists when the repo is mounted read-only. The front page shows the current version.

**Docs.** WSL 2 file-location advice and an engines and licenses note for local parity. The contract suite gap on GitLab and the real image is recorded as an open question. The docs name the real image path instead of placeholders.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-8)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency to 0.5.0 (it is on Packagist).
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update` to take the new template versions for the files you never edited; it shows a diff for the ones you did and never overwrites your edits.
3. Stack repos: regenerate the `deploy/` folder with `squire init` and check it with `squire init --check`. Sourdough: refresh its generated copy with `php bin/export-templates.php --to=templates/squire` and verify it with `--check`.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-8)

Run `squire init --check` and `squire update --dry-run` (the two checks at the top of this page); both exit `0` once the kit is at 0.5.0. New in this version: `squire doctor oracle` answers from your terminal, and a coding agent that runs ADVISOR sees the `squire_doctor` and `squire_drift` tools.

### 0.4.0 (2026-11-01) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-4-0-2026-11-01)

#### Breaking [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-3)

None: the CHANGELOG records no breaking change for 0.4.0.

#### What changed [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-changed-3)

- `oracle-check.php`, a plain-language Oracle connection check (settings, host, port, driver, login), shipped in the kit's deploy scripts. `release.sh` runs it after PROCTOR and before the smoke test; it is a report, never a gate, and stays silent when the app has no `ORACLE_*` settings (see [Oracle](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/oracle.html)).
- Opt-in Oracle-ready Docker images, a Laravel Sail flavor (`squire/oracle-sail`) and a parity flavor (`squire/oracle-parity`), with `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh` and `scripts/oracle-image-test.sh`. Oracle Instant Client 21.7 on amd64 and 19.32 on arm64 is downloaded at build time and checksum-pinned; nothing from Oracle is committed.
- The site's agent-ready files cover the Oracle check.
- The readme art check allows the word Citadel.
- The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local `.env.squire` file is now git-ignored).

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-9)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency to 0.4.0.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update` to take the updated build and release scripts, then `vendor/bin/squire init` to write `oracle-check.php` (this release's `update` refreshed only the files the kit already recorded; `update` writes new files from the next release on).
3. Apps that talk to Oracle: optionally build the Oracle-ready images with `scripts/oracle-image-build.sh` (flavors `sail` and `parity`).

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-9)

Run `squire init --check` and `squire update --dry-run`. Once the kit is at 0.4.0, the app has `oracle-check.php`, and a release log shows the Oracle check after PROCTOR and before the smoke test, printing nothing when the app has no `ORACLE_*` settings.

### 0.3.x (0.3.0 to 0.3.4) [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-x-0-3-0-to-0-3-4)

#### Breaking [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-4)

None: the CHANGELOG records no breaking change in the 0.3.x line.

#### What changed [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#what-changed-4)

- **0.3.4 (2026-10-29).** `squire init` now adds `.env` and `.env.squire` to the target `.gitignore`, so the local deploy secrets file is never committed. The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in `./.env.squire`).
- **0.3.3 (2026-10-29).** `release.sh` reads release options from `./.env.squire` (parsed, never sourced; allow-listed keys; the environment wins), so they can be set on Citadel. The docs say app settings go in a `./.env` configuration file, and the `.env.squire` template says to add it as a Citadel configuration file; Citadel has no dashboard environment field.
- **0.3.2 (2026-10-29).** Collapsed prompt blocks show a "Show the whole prompt" button, and the fade stays inside the panel. A long command in the "Run it in" panel folds the same way, behind a "Show the whole command" button, instead of a scroll box with no cue.
- **0.3.1 (2026-10-29).** README, site and open questions match 0.3.0 (Sourdough requires Squire, the policy default, the Preflight pin, the static target). The agent-ready tool's messages write Squire as a word, and the static template's `SQUIRE_STATIC_ROOT` comment matches the code. `bin/agent-ready.php` is clean under Pint's laravel preset (CI checks it), and the README says how consumers keep the kit out of Composer downloads.
- **0.3.0 (2026-10-29).** The raw target ships a front controller.

#### Steps [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-10)

1. Update the `waynestate/squire` dev dependency to 0.3.4, the latest of the line.
2. Run `vendor/bin/squire update` to take the new template versions for the files you never edited.
3. If your app predates the line, run `vendor/bin/squire init` so the new template files land (for example the raw target's front controller from 0.3.0); `init` never overwrites a file you edited.
4. On Citadel, set the release options in the app's `./.env.squire` configuration file, which `release.sh` reads from 0.3.3 on.

#### How to verify [#](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-10)

Run `squire init --check` and `squire update --dry-run`. Check the version-specific results: 0.3.4 appends `.env` and `.env.squire` to the target `.gitignore` when they are missing; 0.3.3 reads release options from `./.env.squire`; 0.3.0 gives a raw PHP app the front controller `public/index.php`.

Releases before 0.3.0 (0.2.x and 0.1.0) predate this page; their entries are in [Changelog](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html).
